author: Sahil Kurup
title: NFL privately admits enormous refereeing error with huge playoff implications - NewsBreak
text:
By Sahil Kurup ,
26 minutes ago The NFL privately acknowledged a significant officiating mistake after Sunday’s game between the Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints, an error that carried major playoff implications in a tightly contested NFC South race.
Late in the fourth quarter, with the game tied 17–17 with just over two minutes remaining, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young, who suffered a tough injury earlier in the season , connected with rookie wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan on a 12-yard gain near midfield.
The play was ruled a catch on the field, giving Carolina a critical first down as it attempted to set up a potential game-winning drive. New Orleans challenged the call, and after replay review, officials overturned the ruling, changing it to an incomplete pass.

According to a ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio , the NFL later admitted privately to the Panthers that the replay reversal was incorrect.
The league conceded that the original ruling should not have been overturned because the video evidence did not meet the “clear and obvious” standard required to reverse a call on the field.
The play itself quickly became another flashpoint in the league’s long-running confusion surrounding the catch rule. McMillan secured the ball with both hands while going to the ground, with one knee down.
As the ball contacted the turf, his left hand came off, but the football remained controlled in his right hand and never visibly shifted.
Under Rule 3, Section 2, Article 7 of the NFL rulebook, a catch is defined as securing control before the ball touches the ground and maintaining that control throughout the process.
Despite that standard, replay officials ruled the pass incomplete. FOX rules analyst Mike Pereira defended the decision during the broadcast, saying, “He used the ground to complete the catch. He’s going to the ground, and the ball hits the ground. Yes, he had it in control initially, but the bottom hand comes off the ball and they changed it, kept this as an incomplete pass.”
The league office ultimately disagreed with that interpretation. While acknowledging the ruling privately, the NFL confirmed that there was not enough evidence to overturn the call, meaning the first down should have stood.
Although Carolina converted on the following play to keep the drive alive, the reversal removed a crucial first down during a pivotal moment. The Panthers eventually failed to score and later lost 20–17 on a Saints field goal in the closing seconds.
The loss dropped Carolina into a tie with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers atop the NFC South at 7–7. Tampa Bay holds the tiebreaker based on record in common games, making the margin for error razor thin.
With the Panthers and Buccaneers scheduled to face each other twice over the final three weeks of the season, every possession, and every officiating decision, now carries heightened importance.
